name: Oxford
summary: Oxford's honey-stone colleges, libraries and chapels have trained scholars for over 800 years. You can walk its quads and cloisters, see the great museums for free, go punting on the river, and visit Blenheim Palace just outside town.
seasonNote: Spring and summer are loveliest; some colleges close to visitors during exams (May and June). Term time is livelier; August is busy with tourists.
arrival: Trains from London Paddington or Marylebone take about an hour; coaches run from London and Heathrow around the clock.
gettingAround: Walk or rent a bike; park-and-ride buses come into the centre.
cashTip: Cards and tap payments work almost everywhere, even for small amounts; tipping about 10 to 12.5 percent in restaurants is common if service isn't included.
foodTip: The Covered Market's cafés and pies, afternoon tea, and pints in historic pubs.
buyTip: College scarves, Blackwell's books and Oxford University merchandise.
